summary: A [sectoral digital economy policy 2026-2030 was validated and referred to the Council of Ministers](2026-08-04-drc-kibassa-launches-digital-economy-policy-and-national-ai-strategy), uncosted and unpublished.
developments:
2026-08-04 - the policy was [presented and validated by government on axes covering infrastructure, digital transformation of the administration, the digital economy, innovation and start-ups, cybersecurity and data governance, and referred to the Council of Ministers for adoption](2026-08-04-drc-kibassa-launches-digital-economy-policy-and-national-ai-strategy). It is not published, not costed and not budgetable, and the [validators' own conditions name what is missing: reliable baseline data and a completed costing](2026-07-24-drc-psen-2026-2030-expert-validation).

Behind it sits a [national digital plan carrying a US$1.5bn envelope, US$1bn of treasury investment over five years plus US$500m of external partner support](2026-02-20 DRC operationalises $500m partner tranche of PNN2 financing (World Bank, AFD)); no finalised plan document is locatable and the treasury half is an announcement rather than an appropriation.

2026-07-29 - a [governance framework was launched with a ten-dimension maturity diagnostic and a proposed six-to-twelve-month timetable](2026-07-31-drc-digital-maturity-diagnostic-recommendations-governance).

summary: A [National Connectivity Strategy 2026-2035 was published with a target of 3,000 localities and 16 million people by 2030](2026-08-13-drc-fdsu-connectivity-strategy-operator-subsidies).
developments:
2026-08-13 - the strategy was published on a shared-infrastructure model led by a tower company, [with subsidy agreements signed with the four mobile operators to extend service to 40 underserved localities covering about 258,000 people, against a target of 3,000 localities and 16 million people by 2030](2026-08-13-drc-fdsu-connectivity-strategy-operator-subsidies).

The fund publishes its selection framework: a [100-point priority index weighting strategic class 30, coverage deficit 20, population density 15, public infrastructure 15, local economic potential 10 and feasibility 10, with localities above 60 points classed for immediate deployment, subsidy confined to sites where an operator shows a negative return over four years, and national roaming imposed on sites above 70](2026-08-13-drc-fdsu-connectivity-strategy-scoring-framework). The [strategy text is not held](2026-08-14-dr-congo-plans-national-strategy-to-expand-mobile-coverage-in-underserved-areas), and the index did not select the first 40 localities.

progress: No change, a first appearance in the record with nothing earlier behind it
summary: A [sovereign government cloud is named among ministry projects to be ordered and made executable](2026-07-29-drc-kibassa-launches-strategic-framework-digital-transformation), with no hosting location or operator stated.
developments:
2026-07-29 - the sovereign cloud was [named as an existing ministry project alongside the digital and data strategies, the identity platform and a certification authority, with no hosting location, operator, procurement, budget line or date stated](2026-07-29-drc-kibassa-launches-strategic-framework-digital-transformation).

The base carries no statement about a sovereign cloud before that date, so its opening position is unknown rather than zero and no direction can be stated. What exists in the meantime is a budget line for a national data centre and two privately owned facilities, neither of them a state cloud, and no hosting, classification or residency rule to govern what would sit in one.

progress: No change, the framework and the architecture are still deliverables of a consultant not yet appointed
summary: The [e-government strategy's master plan, governance framework, enterprise architecture and interoperability framework are all still to be defined by a consultant](2026-05-06-drc-seeks-consultant-digital-transformation-dpi-biometricupdate).
developments:
The strategy is [named but not operational: its strategic priorities, master plan, governance framework, enterprise architecture and interoperability framework are all still to be defined by a consultant not yet appointed](2026-05-06-drc-seeks-consultant-digital-transformation-dpi-biometricupdate).

It is dated 2025 to 2030 and its defining work was still being tendered in mid-2026, which is the whole of the movement here. No standard, reference architecture or connection obligation on any public body exists on file, and the minister's July 2026 statement of common bases on a national architecture reference framework is the same object restated at ministerial level with nothing built.

summary: A [national AI strategy was validated at a Kinshasa ceremony on 4 August 2026](2026-08-05-rdc-unesco-snia-psen-validation).
developments:
[The Strategie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle and the sectoral digital economy policy were validated at a ceremony in Kinshasa on 4 August 2026, developed with UNESCO support including an AI Readiness Assessment Methodology report](2026-08-05-rdc-unesco-snia-psen-validation). [A mixed AI commission had been created by order in October 2025](2025-10-22-rdc-arrete-cmsnia-commission-mixte-ia).

Validated is not adopted: no decree bringing either instrument into force is held, and neither text was reachable.

summary: A [national data governance strategy was validated and handed to government on 13 November 2025](2025-11-13-rdc-sngd-strategie-nationale-gouvernance-donnees-eca).
developments:
[The Strategie Nationale de Gouvernance des Donnees was nationally validated and formally handed to the government on 13 November 2025 after a three-day ECA-led process, on six pillars: institutional leadership, the legal, regulatory and ethical framework, interoperability and data infrastructure, security and integrity of critical data systems, data skills and literacy, and evidence-based use of data; the digital economy ministry named a national implementation committee as the next step](2025-11-13-rdc-sngd-strategie-nationale-gouvernance-donnees-eca).

No decree adopting the strategy is held, so it is validated rather than in force, and no implementation committee is reported constituted.

summary: The Digital Code is [now enforced on the state's own initiative, prosecutors instructed to open cases without a complaint](2026-08-17-acp-drc-judicial-police-digital-offences).
developments:
The 2023 framework law was in force at the window's opening, its third book governing personal data, with [no data-protection authority operational](2026-04-21-ouvrage-protection-donnees-personnelles-actualite).

2026-08-17 - the attorney general at the Court of Cassation [instructed judicial police officers to open Digital Code cases on their own initiative and forward them for summary hearing](2026-08-17-acp-drc-judicial-police-digital-offences), and the audiovisual regulator's president is [contemplating closing a video platform outright after it did not act on a request to block more than 2,000 accounts](2026-08-19-radiookapi-faut-il-fermer-tiktok-rdc).

The enforcement now running is criminal rather than regulatory: the law's personal-data book has no supervisor, so what has moved is prosecution under it, not protection through it.

summary: A [bill on the identification of natural persons was tabled at the National Assembly bureau on 12 June 2026](2026-06-12-proposition-loi-identification-personnes-physiques-actualite).
developments:
2026-06-12 - the bill was [tabled: it would set one legal frame for identification data and its collection, processing, retention and protection, impose security and interoperability requirements, and connect civil-registry, migration and health databases](2026-06-12-proposition-loi-identification-personnes-physiques-actualite). No committee report or plenary date is held.

It runs alongside rather than through the twenty-year identity concession already signed, and nothing on file connects the two. A statutory frame arriving after the platform it would govern is the sequence here, and no source states which would prevail on retention, access or foreign processing.

summary: Draft ordonnances-lois organising statistical activity were adopted, the country's first legislation on the subject ([adoption](2026-08-29-cod-ordonnance-loi-statistique)).
developments: The Council of Ministers adopted draft ordonnances-lois organising statistical activity on 28 August 2026, presented as the country's first legislation on the subject and as adapting the legal and institutional framework ([adoption](2026-08-29-cod-ordonnance-loi-statistique)). The texts are drafts adopted by the executive; the base holds no promulgation and no published text.

progress: Mixed, an access-to-information bill was declared admissible while a four-level classification regime was put to the Council of Ministers
summary: A [bill setting access as the norm was declared admissible on 27 March 2026](2026-03-28-proposition-loi-acces-information-recevable-actualite); a [classification regime was presented two weeks earlier](2026-03-20-regime-classification-documents-officiels-actualite).
developments:
2026-03-27 - the bill was [declared admissible and referred to a joint commission with ten days to report: it sets access as the norm and limitation the exception, applies to public services and some private actors, and requires a simple, fast and free request procedure, proactive publication, reasoned refusals and a right of appeal](2026-03-28-proposition-loi-acces-information-recevable-actualite). Four months past that ten-day deadline, no commission report, plenary date or adoption is held.

2026-03-13 - an information note to the Council of Ministers set out [four levels of classification with access limited to cleared agents, traceability of transmissions, reinforced archiving and a ban on sending sensitive documents over private messaging](2026-03-20-regime-classification-documents-officiels-actualite), tied by its own account to the security situation in the east.

progress: Mixed, a national network of data-protection officers was launched while the authority the code requires is still not created
summary: A [network of data-protection officers launched in March 2026](2026-03-17-drc-launches-data-protection-officers-network-techafricanews), while the [authority required by article 262 is still not created](2026-07-30-rdc-chaine-responsabilite-visible-cybersecurite).
developments:
The authority is required by article 262 of the code and [the decree defining its organisation and functioning was never drafted or signed, leaving the body non-operational](2024-08-07 RDC - government urged to operationalise the Data Protection Authority) - now two years of the same finding, running alongside a twenty-year exclusive foreign concession over citizens' identity data. It was [named again in July 2026 as a link in the cybersecurity chain](2026-07-30-rdc-chaine-responsabilite-visible-cybersecurite).

2026-03-12 - a [national network of data-protection officers was launched with two civil-society bodies, framed as alignment with the continental convention](2026-03-16-rdc-reseau-responsables-protection-des-donnees-wearetech). It is the first concrete step under article 262 since 2023, and it moves the enforcement gap without closing it: a professional network is not a supervisor with sanctioning powers.

summary: A [drone and citizen-reporting deployment runs in Kinshasa through a private company](2026-01-01-kinshasa-drones-kin-alerte-rdcmonde), and a [ministry memorandum names digital identity in scope](2026-08-13-drc-equity-bcdc-digital-economy-ministry-mou).
developments:
2026-01 - a [drone surveillance and citizen-reporting deployment was reported, operated through a private company, with the reporting outlet itself raising privacy and operator-integrity concerns and no procurement value, legal basis, data-retention rule or oversight arrangement held](2026-01-01-kinshasa-drones-kin-alerte-rdcmonde).

2026-08-13 - the digital economy ministry [signed a memorandum with a commercial bank to modernise financial services and accelerate banking inclusion, covering digital identity and artificial-intelligence integration](2026-08-13-drc-equity-bcdc-digital-economy-ministry-mou), with no term, value, workplan or data-protection provision published.

Both process personal data, neither states a safeguard, and no supervisor exists to ask.

summary: The [African Telecommunications Union's return to Kinshasa was ratified on 23 July 2026](2026-08-12-panafricanpress-atu-drc-mpanda-telecom-milestones) after arrears were paid.
developments:
2026-07-23 - the union's seventh Plenipotentiary Conference [ratified the return of its headquarters to Kinshasa after arrears were paid, with no date for the move stated, and a bid for an ITU Administrative Council seat for 2027-2030 pending](2026-08-12-panafricanpress-atu-drc-mpanda-telecom-milestones).

The arrears figure and the account are the posts and telecommunications minister's own, given marking a year in office, and no union document, decision text or move timetable is held. Hosting a continental body is the clearest regional position the base records for this country in the window.

summary: A [regional free-roaming resolution mandating implementation by 30 June 2026 passed its deadline](2026-02-24-trb-artac-10th-ordinary-session-kinshasa-ngso-techreviewafrica) with nothing on record.
developments:
2026-02-24 - regional regulators [adopted a resolution mandating effective free roaming across Central Africa by 30 June 2026](2026-02-24-trb-artac-10th-ordinary-session-kinshasa-ngso-techreviewafrica), at a session hosted in Kinshasa.

The deadline has passed with no implementation, tariff or country-specific measure held. Nothing states whether Congolese operators were consulted, what a compliant tariff would look like, or what follows a missed regional deadline; the resolution is the only harmonisation instrument on this ledger and it has produced nothing measurable.

summary: A [fibre route linking Goma to Mombasa was reported lit](2026-02-09-paratus-goma-mombasa-fibre-highway-itweb), and a [cable across Lake Tanganyika to Tanzania](2026-09-05-tanzania-drc-tanganyika-fibre-sgr-dailynews) is to be fast-tracked.
developments:
2026-02 - the route was [reported lit, tying eastern DR Congo into the East African terrestrial corridor to the Indian Ocean](2026-02-09-paratus-goma-mombasa-fibre-highway-itweb).

The event date is not separately established from the publication date and both held accounts are trade press. No capacity, pricing, operator agreement or traffic figure is published, and the route serves the same eastern provinces where mobile and internet service has been cut for months at a time, so what it delivers on the ground is not established by anything on file.

2026-09 - the two foreign ministries [reaffirmed that they would fast-track a fibre-optic cable from Kigoma to Kalemie through Lake Tanganyika, alongside a railway link through Burundi and a joint economic commission](2026-09-05-tanzania-drc-tanganyika-fibre-sgr-dailynews). No route survey, cost, financing or delivery date is published, and no Congolese ministry statement is on file.

summary: A regional expert panel [recommended terrestrial gateways inside the region and citizens' data kept on the continent](2026-02-24-trb-artac-10th-ordinary-session-kinshasa-ngso-techreviewafrica), at a session hosted in Kinshasa.
developments:
2026-02-24 - the panel [recommended that non-geostationary satellite providers establish terrestrial gateways within the region's jurisdiction, meet obligations equivalent to traditional operators and keep citizens' data on the continent](2026-02-24-trb-artac-10th-ordinary-session-kinshasa-ngso-techreviewafrica).

It is a recommendation, not an adopted instrument, and the country is the host rather than its author. No national rule on transferring personal data abroad exists on this ledger, which matters because the identity platform running here is operated under a twenty-year concession by a foreign party and no source states where its data sits.

summary: The regulator installed service-quality monitoring equipment and the minister ordered operators to return units consumed without justification ([order](2026-08-27-cod-operateurs-indemniser-abonnes-qos)).
developments: The posts and telecommunications minister ordered the four mobile operators to return units and megabytes consumed abnormally or unjustifiably by their subscribers ([order](2026-08-27-cod-operateurs-indemniser-abonnes-qos)), after inspecting monitoring equipment acquired to trace service-quality failures ([inspection](2026-08-27-cod-radiookapi-arptc-equipements-qos)).

summary: The [Kinshasa carrier-neutral facility holds information-security, continuity and payment-card certifications](2025-02-03-oadc-texaf-kinshasa-iso-pci-dss-certifications-techafricanews), unchanged in the window.
developments:
The facility has been [live since August 2024 as the country's first Tier III certified data centre, certified to information-security, continuity and payment-card standards](2025-02-03-oadc-texaf-kinshasa-iso-pci-dss-certifications-techafricanews), and now [also hosts the internet exchange's second presence](2026-05-19-distributed-exchange-acix-boosts-drc-connectivity-itweb).

The certifications are not re-verified in the base and no recertification date is held. They are also the only international standards adopted by anything on this ledger: no national standards body, conformity regime or certification requirement appears anywhere, so a private facility's commercial certifications are the whole of the position.

summary: A [standing state-industry consultation mechanism was agreed on 6 August 2026](2026-08-07-drc-digital-tax-decree-does-not-cover-startups-industry-body) after the dispute over the digital-sector tariff.
developments:
2026-08-06 - a working session between the digital economy minister and the sector network [agreed a permanent consultation framework after the dispute over the digital-sector tariff, and announced a strategic barometer to give government figures on firms' scope of activity, turnover, growth and job creation](2026-08-07-drc-digital-tax-decree-does-not-cover-startups-industry-body).

No constituting text, membership or meeting schedule is stated for the framework, and no operator, methodology or first-issue date for the barometer. Both were proposed by the industry body rather than instituted by the state, and both follow a tariff dispute in which an order took effect, was said to be suspended, and was then said not to be.

summary: The Council of Ministers [adopted a government-wide strategy against abusive platform content](2026-08-30-rdc-strategie-protection-espace-informationnel) on 28 August 2026, with a citizen alert mechanism and a review of regulation.
developments:
The strategy was adopted at the Council's 97th session and carries an interministerial task force chaired by the communication ministry, a citizen alert mechanism, integration of media literacy into the school curriculum, and a technical and legal review of how the sector is regulated ([strategy](2026-08-30-rdc-strategie-protection-espace-informationnel)).

The strategy text is not held; what is held is the Council's own account of what it adopted. Neither the account nor anything else on file defines abusive content, names who decides, or says what follows a citizen alert.

It lands on a base that already records the digital code being enforced on the state's own initiative, with the attorney general instructing judicial police officers to open cases proprio motu ([code](2026-08-17-acp-drc-judicial-police-digital-offences)). A reporting channel and a prosecutorial instruction are the two halves of the same mechanism.

progress: Mixed, both digital sections were appropriated higher for FY2026 while the rise is substantially a transfer of mandate and only 51.7% of the prior year's credit was paid
summary: The [digital economy section rose to FC 81,698,223,741 for FY2026](2025-12-29-cod-2026-71), but [only 51.7% of the FY2025 revised credit was paid](2025-06-28-cod-2025-71).
developments:
The 2026 finance law [renamed the digital section digital economy and appropriated FC 81,698,223,741 domestic, up 34.8% on FY2025 and still 6.2% below the FY2024 appropriation](2025-12-29-cod-2026-71), and [renamed the other section posts and telecommunications at FC 53,840,917,417](2025-12-29-cod-2026-52). [Credits moved from FC 145.7bn to FC 55.1bn on one section and from FC 60.6bn to FC 226.7bn on the other](2025-12-29-cod-2026-52), so combined the two are almost flat and the rise is substantially a transfer of mandate.

Execution is the weak point: [FC 31,358,784,468 was paid, 51.7% of the revised credit, against FC 68,457,537,329 engaged, or 112.9%](2025-06-28-cod-2025-71). National identification received [FC 20,654,178 for FY2026](2026-05-29-cod-actualitecd-onip-identification-nationale-ppp), a figure that cross-foots exactly and is not a transcription error.

summary: The central bank [signed a card-network memorandum on payments and inclusion](2026-04-16-visa-bcc-agreement-financial-inclusion-payments-techafricanews), and the [digital ministry signed one with a commercial bank](2026-08-13-drc-equity-bcdc-digital-economy-ministry-mou).
developments:
2026-04 - the central bank governor and a card-network executive [signed a memorandum on three pillars: technical capacity building, financial inclusion and literacy, and secure resilient payment systems, aligned to the bank's 2026-2030 plan](2026-04-16-visa-bcc-agreement-financial-inclusion-payments-techafricanews). No monetary value is attached and the signing date is not given separately from the report date.

2026-08-13 - the digital economy ministry [signed with a commercial bank on modernising financial services and accelerating banking inclusion, covering digital identity and artificial-intelligence integration under the 2019 national digital plan and the 2023 Digital Code](2026-08-13-drc-equity-bcdc-digital-economy-ministry-mou), with no term, value or workplan published.

summary: A [US$179m upsized senior facility funds 728 new towers](2026-08-05-eaaif-eastcastle-liquid-82m-eaif), alongside a [US$100m investment convention](2026-03-31-anapi-helios-towers-investissement-actualite).
developments:
The base's earlier position was a [US$30m commitment in 2023 supporting tower purchase and development, with the network at 1,072 active towers](2023-01-01-pidg-cod-eastcastle-2023-eastcastle-drc-telecom-tower-platform).

2026-08-05 - a development fund [committed US$32.8m inside an upsized US$179m senior secured facility funding 728 new passive towers to take the network to 1,800, 70% of them rural, plus solar and battery upgrades](2026-08-05-eaaif-eastcastle-liquid-82m-eaif). A [further US$34.35m debt facility to the same recipient sits at pipeline stage](2026-07-16-iati-xm-dac-903-sii-52276-eastcastle-drc-telecom-towers), and whether the two are linked is not established.

2026-03-31 - a separate tower operator [signed an investment convention of more than US$100m with the investment-promotion agency, stating more than 4,000 jobs already created](2026-03-31-anapi-helios-towers-investissement-actualite); the convention text and any disbursement figure are not held.

summary: A [US$200m IDA additional financing was adopted in draft ratifying ordinance-law on 14 August 2026](2026-08-17-transforme-rdc-ida-200m-additional-financing-lobito).
developments:
2026-08-14 - the Council of Ministers [adopted a draft ordinance-law ratifying a US$200m IDA additional financing extending the enterprise project into the Lobito corridor, its loan agreement concluded on 22 June 2026, taking the parent project approved in 2022 at US$300m to US$500m in total](2026-08-17-transforme-rdc-ida-200m-additional-financing-lobito). The [financier's own project paper splits the US$200m into a US$176m credit and a US$24m credit](2026-06-05-world-bank-transforme-drc-additional-financing-project-paper). The ordinance-law is not promulgated and no disbursement is on record.

2026-08-07 - a separate financial-sector package [announced a modernised credit-risk registry and an electronic movable-collateral registry to be built with the central bank, alongside a deposit-guarantee fund and 10,000 point-of-sale terminals](2026-08-07-drc-world-bank-sme-finance-digitalization), with no instrument, custodian or timetable stated.

summary: Mobile subscriptions reached [73.93m at 67.8% penetration in 2025, from 63.96m and 60.5% in 2024](2026-08-03-eaco-regional-communications-sector-statistics-report-2025).
developments:
The first regulator-submitted regional dataset the base holds puts the country at [73.93m mobile subscriptions and 67.8% penetration in 2025, against 63.96m and 60.5% in 2024](2026-08-03-eaco-regional-communications-sector-statistics-report-2025).

It is a regional compilation of the national regulator's own returns rather than a published national series, and the regulator itself publishes nothing comparable that the base holds. The same return reports no mobile-money transaction value at all, so a country with tens of millions of wallets contributes no payment volume to the regional statistics it now files into.

The next generation is not moving: a [public consultation on introducing 5G opened in March 2025](2025-03-18-arptc-consultation-publique-5g-actualite) and seventeen months later no consultation report, spectrum award, licence or revised timetable has been published.

summary: Mobile-internet subscriptions stand at [36.98m, 33.9% penetration, with mobile-internet revenue of US$970.2m in 2025](2026-08-03-eaco-regional-communications-sector-statistics-report-2025).
developments:
The regional dataset records [36.98m mobile-internet subscriptions at 33.9% penetration and mobile-internet revenue of US$970.2m in 2025, nearly matching voice revenue](2026-08-03-eaco-regional-communications-sector-statistics-report-2025).

The earlier position the base holds is a Council of Ministers record of [30.79% mobile-internet access and under 0.02% fixed access](2025-06-22-tshisekedi-fracture-numerique-conseil-ministres-actualite), which is close enough to the 2025 figure to say the level is stated rather than a movement measured. Fixed access remains statistically absent, and no household or individual usage survey exists on this ledger.

summary: Bundle validity was cut without notice: [1GB at 1,500 francs fell from 48 hours to 24](2026-08-15-drc-bukavu-internet-tariff-complaints), and the 2GB bundle was replaced.
developments:
Subscribers in Bukavu and the eastern provinces report that [a 1GB bundle at 1,500 Congolese francs, formerly valid 48 hours, is now valid 24 hours, and a 2GB bundle at 2,000 francs valid 48 hours has been replaced by 1GB valid 72 hours at the same price](2026-08-15-drc-bukavu-internet-tariff-complaints).

Both ends are [subscribers' and resellers' accounts](2026-08-15-drc-subscriber-tariff-complaints-east-drc); no operator or regulator statement is on record and the changes are reported as unannounced. It is the only affordability evidence on this ledger, and it comes from the same eastern provinces where service has been cut outright for months at a time.

summary: [7,000 km of backbone is deployed against a target of more than 18,500 km](2026-08-03-rdc-11500-km-fibre-optique-restants-ptn), leaving 11,500 km outstanding to 2030.
developments:
2026-08-03 - the 95th ordinary Council meeting was told [7,000 km had been deployed against a target of more than 18,500 km, leaving 11,500 km outstanding, tied to connecting 145 territories by 2030](2026-08-03-rdc-11500-km-fibre-optique-restants-ptn). The [minister cites budget constraints and a low disbursement rate on external financing, and the remaining distance over the 2030 horizon implies about 2,900 km a year against about 7,000 km delivered in the programme's first year](2026-08-03-rdc-11500-km-fibre-optique-restants-ptn).

2026-07 - a [memorandum was signed with a Chinese supplier for about 2,100 km along and beside the Congo River at a stated US$1.5bn, more than US$400m of it required for the first phase](2026-07-03-drc-plans-1-5bn-fibre-congo-river-genew-connectingafrica), with no financing close, contract or works. Both figures are company-reported.

summary: One exchange [became distributed across two carrier-neutral facilities](2026-05-19-distributed-exchange-acix-boosts-drc-connectivity-itweb) and another [moved into a Tier III facility](2026-08-20-drc-kinix-internet-exchange-relocates-to-raxio-drc).
developments:
2026-05 - an exchange established in 2023 and operating from a single presence [added a second presence at a Kinshasa carrier-neutral facility, making it the country's first distributed exchange, open to licensed operators, service providers, mobile networks, cloud and content providers](2026-05-19-distributed-exchange-acix-boosts-drc-connectivity-itweb).

2026-08-20 - a second exchange [relocated its infrastructure into a carrier-neutral Tier III data centre, the operators stating it connects more than 20 networks with over 1 Tbps of available capacity and expecting more than 2 Tbps after the move, as one of three points under a national exchange project managed by the internet service providers association](2026-08-20-drc-kinix-internet-exchange-relocates-to-raxio-drc). Capacity and network counts are the operators' own and no traffic measurement is held for either.

progress: Mixed, a satellite-to-mobile service launched commercially while the sovereign satellite programme did not move in twelve months
summary: A [satellite direct-to-cell service launched commercially on 14 August 2026](2026-08-18-airtel-starlink-satellite-mobile-drc), while the [sovereign satellite programme is unchanged](2025-08-31-projet-acquisition-satellite-monacosat-actualite).
developments:
The satellite provider has been [licensed since May 2025, reversing a March 2024 prohibition](2025-05-02-starlink-licence-officielle-actualite), a decision [civil society welcomed as a corrective to incumbent monopoly abuse](2025-05-05-acaj-salue-homologation-starlink-actualite); the licence conditions and any enforcement outcome are not established.

2026-08-14 - a [satellite-to-mobile service launched commercially, the first African operator to take such a partnership out of testing: a compatible handset with a clear view of the sky reaches messaging and voice where there is no terrestrial coverage, with no dish or router, on a phased rollout the regulator has confirmed](2026-08-18-airtel-starlink-satellite-mobile-drc). A [free 30-day trial is the only access term published](2026-08-14-drc-airtel-starlink-direct-to-cell-numerico).

The [sovereign satellite programme has no contract, operator selection, build or launch date twelve months on](2025-08-31-projet-acquisition-satellite-monacosat-actualite).

summary: The [largest facility is unchanged at 400 racks, 1,542 square metres and 1.5 MW](2025-10-31-mbtp-raxio-datacenter-actualite); only its parent's capital moved.
developments:
The facility has [operated since August 2024 as the country's largest, Tier III certified, at 400 racks over 1,542 square metres and 1.5 MW, on US$30m invested](2025-10-31-mbtp-raxio-datacenter-actualite). No utilisation, capacity-sold or expansion figure is held, and its position did not move in the window.

What moved is its parent's balance sheet: [committed capital rose from US$350m to US$380m, with six times as much power contracted in the first half of 2026 as a year earlier](2026-07-15 Raxio data-centre capital tops $380m on investor boost). That is group-level across six live markets and none of it is allocated to this country in the source, so it says nothing about capacity here.

summary: The enacted 2026 finance law [carries FC 26,756,546,346 for national data-centre acquisition](2025-12-29-cod-2026-71), with no procurement or site held.
developments:
No national data-centre appropriation is established at the window's opening. The [enacted 2026 budget carries FC 26,756,546,346 for national data-centre acquisition](2025-12-29-cod-2026-71).

No procurement, site, operator, specification or execution evidence is held, and no 2026 execution data has been published at all, so an appropriation is the whole of it. Set against the prior year's payment rate of just over half the revised credit on the same section, an appropriation on this line is a weaker signal here than it would be elsewhere.

summary: [22 of the rural electrification agency's 65 plants moved into the operating phase](2026-02-02-anser-22-centrales-phase-exploitation).
developments:
[22 of ANSER's 65-project portfolio of rural power plants moved from construction into the operating phase, after a ministerial order validated in Council made the agency the contracting authority able to recruit private operators for exploitation and maintenance](2026-02-02-anser-22-centrales-phase-exploitation). [Its Mwinda Fund became operational in October 2025](2025-10-06-anser-mwinda-fund-operationnel).

This is rural generation rather than a supply position for telecom sites or data centres, which the base still does not state.

summary: A [public-administration reference file went to procurement](2026-08-19-laprosperite-coref-frap-marche-brondy), and a [2026-2028 public-enterprise digitalisation plan was disseminated](2026-07-16-igf-digitalisation-entreprises-publiques-rdcmonde).
developments:
2026-08-19 - the public finance reform committee [notified its intention to award the equipment lot for a public-administration reference file and opened the standstill period, funded by an IDA credit and grant](2026-08-19-laprosperite-coref-frap-marche-brondy). The notice carries no contract value and does not describe what the reference file will hold.

2026-07-15 - a [dissemination seminar opened on a 2026-2028 public-enterprise plan with digitalisation as its backbone, covering transaction traceability, automated validation circuits, real-time alerts and data reconciliation across state enterprises](2026-07-16-igf-digitalisation-entreprises-publiques-rdcmonde); no system, budget line or deployment date is named.

summary: A [presidential ordinance of 16 May 2026 creates the national cybersecurity agency](2026-05-16-rdc-ancy-ordonnance-26-033-journal-officiel).
developments:
[Ordonnance 26-033, signed on 16 May 2026 and published in the Journal Officiel, creates the Agence Nationale de Cybersecurite under the 2023 Digital Code, with powers to audit public institutions and operators of vital importance and to certify and homologate cybersecurity products and services, and tasks it with standing up a national security operations centre and a CERT; covered entities must notify it of attacks and intrusions](2026-05-16-rdc-ancy-ordonnance-26-033-journal-officiel).

It is the clearest movement from legal framework to institution the base holds. Neither the operations centre nor the CERT is reported operating, and no incident report or advisory from the agency is on the record.

progress: No change, both the exchange platform and the certification authority are named on paper with nothing built
summary: A [data-sharing platform and payment gateway are consultant deliverables](2026-05-06-drc-seeks-consultant-digital-transformation-dpi-biometricupdate), and a [certification authority is named but not established](2026-07-29-drc-kibassa-launches-strategic-framework-digital-transformation).
developments:
The platform and gateway are [specified on paper only: no architecture, pilot, operator or date, and the interoperability framework is itself a consultant deliverable](2026-05-06-drc-seeks-consultant-digital-transformation-dpi-biometricupdate).

The [electronic certification authority is named among the instruments to be articulated into the governance framework but is not established, while a July 2026 interministerial order already prices qualified trust services at US$30,000 foreign and US$10,000 local](2026-07-29-drc-kibassa-launches-strategic-framework-digital-transformation). A fee schedule exists before the institution does.

Neither had a position in the base at the window's opening, so what is stated is where they now stand rather than a direction.

summary: The [national digital identity platform launched on 13 June 2026, valued at US$97.1m](2026-06-15-drc-launches-rdc-pass-20-year-ppp-trident-biometricupdate), with no enrolment figure published.
developments:
At the window's opening a [twenty-year exclusive electronic know-your-customer partnership signed in June 2025 was in phased deployment with no platform live](2025-08-29-drc-digital-id-phased-deployment-contract-do-over-biometricupdate).

2026-06-13 - the platform [launched at a state ceremony, valued at US$97.1m by the planning ministry, with US$2.6m raised by the concessionaire for initial rollout and rollout to begin with technical audits and pilot testing](2026-06-15-drc-launches-rdc-pass-20-year-ppp-trident-biometricupdate). No enrolment figure is published, [and the financing was already unclear when the valuation was reported in January 2026](2026-01-26 DRCPass digital ID priced at $97.1M, financing unclear).

A March 2026 rollout target passed with neither launch nor delay announced before the June launch.

summary: The identification office held its first board meeting and adopted a roadmap to accelerate registration ([roadmap](2026-08-26-cod-onip-feuille-de-route-identification)).
developments:
The national identification office held its first board meeting on 20-21 August 2026 and adopted a roadmap to accelerate population identification ([roadmap](2026-08-26-cod-onip-feuille-de-route-identification)). A roadmap is not enrolment: the base holds no registration figure against it.

At the window's opening a [card-production partner was under discussion with no start date and no financing route](2025-11-16-gouvernement-relance-carte-identite-onip-actualite).

2026-05-29 - the office [announced the start of operations as imminent with the partner withheld, the 2026 finance law giving national-identification acquisition FC 20,654,178 and revised provisions sitting in a supplementary budget before the Assembly](2026-05-29-cod-actualitecd-onip-identification-nationale-ppp).

The last national identification was in 1984. The electoral file was formally handed to the identification office in February 2026, and no enrolment or card-issuance figure is held at either end - so what has moved is the financing route, not the count of people identified.

2026-08-17 - separately, [forty agents finished training at Gbadolite for a provincial operation identifying Mbororo herders, on a digital collection tool and a questionnaire validated by an interministerial commission recording identity, ties to the country, weapons and cattle](2026-08-18-lepotentiel-nord-ubangi-identification-mbororo). No legal basis, retention rule or data controller is stated for it.

progress: No change, the identity layer runs on a twenty-year exclusive concession while the domestic appropriation for identification is negligible
summary: Identification is [run under a twenty-year exclusive partnership](2026-06-15-drc-launches-rdc-pass-20-year-ppp-trident-biometricupdate) while the state appropriated [FC 20,654,178 for it](2025-12-29-cod-2026-71).
developments:
The identity platform operates under a [twenty-year exclusive partnership signed in June 2025](2025-08-29-drc-digital-id-phased-deployment-contract-do-over-biometricupdate), and the state's own appropriation for national identification acquisition in the [enacted 2026 finance law is FC 20,654,178](2025-12-29-cod-2026-71) - a figure that cross-foots exactly against its group total and is not a transcription error.

It corroborates the identification office's own account that the allocation obliged recourse to a partnership. No transfer milestone, revenue share, performance standard, exit arrangement or data-custody rule is published for the twenty-year concession, and no state body is named as holding the register at its end.

2026-08-31 — a Brussels court referred fourteen defendants to trial over the contract under which a Belgian firm produced the country's biometric passports from 2015 to 2025, on charges of bribery of foreign public officials, money laundering and tax fraud; the civil parties, 51 citizens who filed in 2020 with a coalition of anti-corruption organisations, put the diversion at close to US$60 million ([referral](2026-08-31-fidh-cnpav-communique-semlex-renvoi-tribunal-correctionnel), [report](2026-09-01-biometricupdate-semlex-congo-passport-trial)). The identity layer's other credential ran on the same procurement pattern.

summary: [RDC-PASS launched on 13 June 2026 as the national digital identity and authentication platform](2026-06-13-rdc-pass-plateforme-identite-numerique-nationale).
developments:
[RDC-PASS is online following its presidential launch on 13 June 2026, on a phased rollout that trains agents before registering citizens, and lists authentication, electronic signature, document verification and bank and mobile-money identity as its operative service set](2026-06-13-rdc-pass-plateforme-identite-numerique-nationale). [Agent training was under way at launch](2026-06-15-deskeco-rdc-pass-lancement-agents).

No registration count, relying-party count or uptake figure is held, and nothing states how it keys to the general population register.

summary: A rural eastern sector [has had no birth registers for several months and newborn registration has stopped outright](2026-07-25-cd-walikale-registres-naissance-identite).
developments:
2026-07-25 - a sector chief told the provincial interior division that [his civil-status office has had no birth registers for several months, that newborn registration has stopped outright, and that the province promised resupply with no date](2026-07-25-cd-walikale-registres-naissance-identite). The stated consequences are exclusion from school enrolment and from proof of nationality.

It is the concrete measure of how far civil-registry modernisation reaches into rural territories, and it runs in the same year a national digital identity platform launched in Kinshasa. No registration rate, register-stock figure or resupply programme appears anywhere on this ledger.

summary: The [biometric passport stands at US$75, 2,400 a day across 100 stations](2025-06-02-drc-cuts-biometric-passport-price-dermalog-biometricupdate), with no later figure held.
developments:
The passport price was cut to [US$75 with a new supplier and online enrolment, on 50 fixed and mobile stations plus 50 at missions and a stated 2,400 a day](2025-06-02-drc-cuts-biometric-passport-price-dermalog-biometricupdate), against prior prices of US$185 then US$99, under a 2022 contract worth US$48m.

No later price, volume or station figure is held, so the position is unchanged through the window. Nothing states whether the passport draws on, or will draw on, the identity platform launched in June 2026, which is the question the indicator asks and which no held source addresses.

summary: The central bank [set 9 April 2027 as the date from which no foreign-cash transaction of any amount is permitted](2026-05-04-bcc-inclusion-financiere-58-pourcent-actualite).
developments:
2026-05 - the central bank [set 9 April 2027 as the date from which no foreign-cash transaction of any amount is permitted](2026-05-04-bcc-inclusion-financiere-58-pourcent-actualite). The deadline stands with no implementing instrument, exemption schedule or enforcement mechanism held.

It runs directly against the dollar-denominated rails proliferating around it, including a [stablecoin settlement use case live on a card-network partner's rail](2026-04-16-visa-bcc-agreement-financial-inclusion-payments-techafricanews) whose peg is inferred rather than disclosed. No held source reconciles the two, and no supervisory statement addresses what a de-dollarised retail payment system would settle in.

progress: Mixed, a rural payroll route was scoped while Kinshasa's urban administration went two months unpaid and the biometric civil-servant register published no new figure
summary: A [rural payroll arrangement was scoped to three territories](2026-07-25-drc-rural-civil-servant-payroll-technical-harmonisation), while [Kinshasa agents demonstrated over two months of arrears](2026-07-23-drc-kinshasa-public-administration-salary-arrears).
developments:
2026-07 - a state bank and the payroll monitoring committee [settled technical and organisational terms for rural payroll, scoped to three named territories and others where no other bank operates, with August 2026 named as a target, the bank's director-general saying a fixed date is premature, the state contract unsigned and its core banking replacement still in test](2026-07-24-actualitecd-cadeco-csp-paie-proximite-milieu-rural). The [bank's reach is reported at both around 40 sites and about thirty territories](2026-07-25-drc-rural-civil-servant-payroll-technical-harmonisation), and that reach is the whole rationale for the arrangement.

2026-07-23 - Kinshasa urban administration agents [demonstrated over two months of unpaid salary, beneficiary listings already transmitted to the paying bank but neither bank staff nor payroll agents attending the appointed payment](2026-07-23-drc-kinshasa-public-administration-salary-arrears) - a failure at the last mile of an otherwise complete digital chain.

The [biometric civil-servant registry stands at more than 118,000 cards across 26 provinces with no updated figure in twelve months](2025-07-17 DR Congo launches digital civil servant registry to tackle ghost workers (ENCORE)).

summary: Standardised electronic invoicing is [mandatory since 1 December 2025, with quarterly VAT mobilisation up from CFC 280-290bn to CFC 340bn](2026-08-06-cod-facture-normalisee-fwamba).
developments:
The system was initiated in 2017 and operationalised on 1 August 2025. It is [mandatory since 1 December 2025 for all firms liable to VAT after a two-month moratorium and a further 30-day grace period, the state having distributed more than 4,000 free billing units and electronic fiscal devices to liable small and medium firms, with quarterly VAT mobilisation risen from a CFC 280-290bn average to CFC 340bn, which the finance minister still calls very largely below potential](2026-08-06-cod-facture-normalisee-fwamba). Fiscal clinics closed in August 2026 with immediate targeted sanctions ordered against non-compliant taxpayers and revenue staff alike. The figures are the minister's own and unaudited.

2026-06-11 - a province [made electronic payment of an airport levy official from July through a private technical partner with real-time tracking](2026-06-11-ndjili-go-pass-paiement-electronique-rdcmonde); whether it went live is not established.

summary: A [partnership agreement covers connecting microfinance institutions and cooperatives to the national switch across 145 territories](2026-04-16-transforme-paycode-digitalisation-imf-coopec-actualite).
developments:
2026-04 - a payments firm and two sector associations [signed on core banking, enterprise resource planning and card modules, 10,000 payment terminals with biometric authentication, chip cards, and connection of microfinance institutions and cooperatives to the national switch across 145 territories](2026-04-16-transforme-paycode-digitalisation-imf-coopec-actualite).

Nothing is deployed on file. The switch connection is the load-bearing item and no go-live is held; the arrangement is externally financed, and no source names the operator of the switch, the connection standard or what an institution must meet to join.

summary: The state bus operator opened a QR-code ticketing trial in Kinshasa ([trial](2026-08-31-cod-transco-billetterie-electronique-qr)).
developments:
The state bus operator opened a trial of QR-code electronic ticketing in Kinshasa on 31 August 2026 ([trial](2026-08-31-cod-transco-billetterie-electronique-qr)). No fare volume, route coverage or payment provider is named.

The interoperability service has been [live since the fourth quarter of 2025 and is now the rail on which a stablecoin settlement use case runs](2025-09-04 Visa Pay launches to expand digital payments across the DRC); no transaction volume, merchant count or user figure is held.

2026-04-30 - a [palm-vein payment technology launched in Kinshasa, stated as integrated into national payments infrastructure and named against the 2023-2028 financial-inclusion strategy](2026-04-30-mainmoney-palm-vein-lancement-actualite), with [no deployment count or transaction figure](2026-05-11-mainmoney-palm-biometrics-financial-inclusion-drc-biometricupdate).

2026-07-14 - a card network and a domestic payments company [announced physical and virtual prepaid card issuance, the domestic partner serving more than three million customers through 4,000 agents and 160 agencies](2026-07-14-mastercard-flash-digital-financial-inclusion-drc-techafricanews); no issuance date or card volume is stated.

progress: No change, four counts of mobile-money accounts circulate and none is reconcilable to another
summary: The most precisely dated figure is [29m accounts at 34.6% penetration](2026-01-26 How Onafriq is growing digital finance amid uncertainty in DRC); the base holds 24m, 29m, 30m and 35m.
developments:
The only dated, attributable count is [29m accounts and 34.6% penetration, from a payments aggregator's fourth-quarter 2024 figures](2026-01-26 How Onafriq is growing digital finance amid uncertainty in DRC). An [operator cites about 35m users in April 2026](2026-04-03-vodacom-congo-integrated-financial-ecosystem-inclusion-techreviewafrica), and the base holds 24m, 29m, 30m and 35m across sources.

The divergence is the finding: four counts, none reconcilable, and no published central-bank series. The nearest official figure is [about 58% financial inclusion against 25 to 30% bank-account penetration, the gap attributed to mobile-money use without a bank account](2026-05-04-bcc-inclusion-financiere-58-pourcent-actualite), with no earlier dated rate held.

summary: A [live use case settles mobile-wallet top-ups in stablecoins](2026-07-06-visa-mpesa-onafriq-stablecoin-pilot-drc-techafricanews), bypassing correspondent banking.
developments:
2026-07 - a card-network executive [confirmed on record a live use case settling wallet top-ups in stablecoins in the background, bypassing correspondent banking, which carries about 8% of sub-Saharan remittance cost](2026-07-06-visa-mpesa-onafriq-stablecoin-pilot-drc-techafricanews). The [dollar peg is inferred rather than disclosed](2026-07-02 Visa tests stablecoins in DRC for cross-border payments (The EastAfrican)), and a joint pilot-launch framing was downgraded on reconciliation.

It runs against the central bank's own de-dollarisation deadline of April 2027, and no supervisory position, licence or reporting obligation for stablecoin settlement is on file. No corridor volume or value is published.

summary: [Digitalisation of the Kinshasa population register began in November 2025](2025-11-04-radiookapi-debut-digitalisation-registre-population-kinshasa).
developments:
[Digitalisation of the population register began in Kinshasa in November 2025](2025-11-04-radiookapi-debut-digitalisation-registre-population-kinshasa), under the [general population file instituted by Decret 22-07 of 2 March 2022](2022-03-02-decret-22-07-fichier-general-population). [Communal agents were being trained on digitalised enumeration by August 2026](2026-08-10-acp-kasa-vubu-agents-communaux-digitalisation-recensement).

No enrolment count, coverage figure or completion date is held for any commune.

summary: A [single-window portal and application now issue sole-trader attestations in under 48 hours](2026-07-28-cd-guce-formalisation-numerique), but full online company creation is not possible.
developments:
2026-07-28 - a ministerial inspection presented a [portal that proposes a legal form and tracks a file in real time and an application that issues sole-trader attestations in under 48 hours, while full online company creation remains impossible, the chain still spanning the revenue directorate, a collecting bank, the notariat and verification](2026-07-28-cd-guce-formalisation-numerique). The 48-hour figure describes the attestation segment, not the registration process.

2026-08-07 - a financial-sector package [announced a modernised credit-risk registry and an electronic movable-collateral registry to be built with the central bank](2026-08-07-drc-world-bank-sme-finance-digitalization), with no instrument, custodian, timetable or access rule stated, and no data-protection provision reported for the credit file.

summary: A [draft decree creating the single social register was adopted in Council on 25 July 2025](2025-07-27-adoption-decret-registre-social-unique-actualite) and has not been promulgated.
developments:
2025-07-25 - the 53rd Council of Ministers [adopted a draft decree creating and organising the register](2025-07-27-adoption-decret-registre-social-unique-actualite).

Twelve months later there is no signed decree number, signature date or publication, no operator, no household enrolment and no link to the identification office. Adoption in council is not promulgation, and twelve months in the same state is the finding. It would also create a second population register alongside the identification office's, and nothing on file states how the two would relate.

summary: [Loi 25-062 on the land and property regime came into force in December 2025](2025-12-30-rdc-loi-25-062-regime-foncier-immobilier), with a [national land plan to 2040](2026-06-12-affaires-foncieres-plan-foncier-national-2026-2040).
developments:
[Loi 25-062 on the land and property regime was enacted on 30 December 2025](2025-12-30-rdc-loi-25-062-regime-foncier-immobilier). [A national land plan for 2026 to 2040 followed in June 2026](2026-06-12-affaires-foncieres-plan-foncier-national-2026-2040), [a national land and property register went to Senate reform discussion](2026-06-10-affairesfoncieres-senat-reforme-fonciere-rntfi), and [digitalisation of the land registry was reported in August 2026](2026-08-11-apanews-land-registry-digitalisation-inaco).

No parcel count, coverage figure or completion date for the digitalisation is held.

summary: A [higher-education portal and first national digital library went live](2026-04-02-rdc-portail-numerique-universitaire-esursi-wearetech) for student identification, transcripts and equivalences.
developments:
2026-04 - the portal and library [went live under external financing, carrying student identification, transcripts and equivalences](2026-04-02-rdc-portail-numerique-universitaire-esursi-wearetech).

No registration, usage or institution-coverage figure is held, and the scientific-output archive that would make it a research instrument is announced rather than built. It is the only sectoral management system on this ledger with a live date, which places every other sector - health, justice, social protection - at no evidence rather than at a stated position.

summary: The finance inspectorate's [2026-2028 plan makes automated cross-checking of customs, tax, standards and freight records a pillar of systemic control](2026-08-21-congoquotidien-igf-controle-systemique-plan-strategique).
developments:
2026-08-20 - the plan was [disseminated to public administrations, making automated cross-checking of customs, tax, standards and freight-management records a pillar of systemic control](2026-08-21-congoquotidien-igf-controle-systemique-plan-strategique). The inspectorate states that [what limits it is the reliability of the data the administrations produce rather than the technology, and commits to help the revenue agencies improve it](2026-08-18-deskeco-igf-fiabilite-qualite-donnees).

No platform, interface or timetable is named. The [worked example given is a consignment imported at US$10,000 and declared to customs at US$1,000](2026-08-19-lepoint-cd-igf-croiser-donnees-douane-dgi-occ-ogefrem), which is the case cross-checking would catch and which nothing on file shows being caught yet.

summary: [Electronic transmission of the documentary file between the single window and customs became compulsory in January 2026](2026-01-09-rdc-guce-dgda-transmission-electronique-obligatoire).
developments:
[Transmission of the documentary file between the single window and the customs administration became compulsory and electronic in January 2026](2026-01-09-rdc-guce-dgda-transmission-electronique-obligatoire), [after the Prime Minister launched digitalisation of the documentary file in December 2025](2025-12-29-primature-lancement-digitalisation-liasse-documentaire). [Customs run SYDONIA](2022-03-28-dgda-sydonia).

No declaration volume, clearance time or revenue figure from the system is held.

summary: The [digital government platform's first-quarter 2026 target passed with neither launch nor delay announced](2026-05-06-drc-seeks-consultant-digital-transformation-dpi-biometricupdate).
developments:
A [functional digital government platform was targeted for March 2026](2026-01-30 DRC envisages a functional digital government platform by March), announced alongside an interbank payment platform, an online tax portal and a customs system. [No platform, revised date or announced delay is held](2026-05-06-drc-seeks-consultant-digital-transformation-dpi-biometricupdate), and none of the companion systems is established as live.

2026-06-24 - technical training closed for ministry staff on a [platform to authenticate documents against forgery for economic inspections](2026-06-26-economie-nationale-plateforme-e-controle-actualite); training completion is the only milestone on file and whether the platform is in production is not established.

summary: A [state guarantee fund launched an assisted business-plan platform](2026-02-04-bokeli-plateforme-fogec-actualite), and the [employment agency put AI modules out to tender](2026-08-01-drc-enabel-onem-ai-digital-platform-tender).
developments:
2026-02 - a state guarantee fund [launched a public platform giving step-by-step business-plan drafting, financial projections, export and direct submission with real-time file tracking, built by a domestic firm](2026-02-04-bokeli-plateforme-fogec-actualite). No usage figures, model or vendor disclosure and no data-protection arrangement are stated.

2026-08-01 - the national employment agency's existing platform went [out to tender for artificial-intelligence modules to be developed, integrated and deployed, offers due 7 September 2026](2026-08-01-drc-enabel-onem-ai-digital-platform-tender). It is procured by a foreign development agency rather than by the state, and no contract value, award or delivery date is on record.

summary: An award citation records [artificial intelligence used to mark the 2024-25 state examination](2025-11-27-adis-2025-raissa-malu-education-numerique-actualite), alongside electronic diplomas.
developments:
The only sectoral use on file is [artificial intelligence used to mark the 2024-25 state examination, named among the education ministry's reforms alongside electronic diplomas and decentralised scanning centres](2025-11-27-adis-2025-raissa-malu-education-numerique-actualite).

It reaches the base as an award citation. The marking belongs to the 2024-25 session and no date is established for it; no scope, vendor, model, accuracy figure or human-oversight arrangement is held. A national examination marked by machine with no published accuracy check and no appeal route stated is the position as the base holds it.

summary: A [Lingala training-data collection project launched in August 2026](2026-08-07-drc-digital-code-public-awareness-campaign-launched), and a [student facility was announced](2026-02-20-drc-500m-digital-transformation-world-bank-afd-techafricanews).
developments:
2026-08-06 - the digital economy ministry [launched a project with UN development programme support to build Lingala training data for artificial-intelligence models](2026-08-07-drc-digital-code-public-awareness-campaign-launched); no corpus size, licence, host or publication date is stated.

2026-02-20 - a [student artificial-intelligence facility was announced alongside state-data migration and a government cybersecurity centre](2026-02-20-drc-500m-digital-transformation-world-bank-afd-techafricanews), with no design, budget line, site or date established and the event date itself unestablished.

Both are announcements. No compute, model, dataset or research output exists anywhere on this ledger, so the country's artificial-intelligence capability is a strategy, an academy on paper and a language corpus not yet collected.

progress: No change, a first statement of the institutional position with nothing earlier behind it
summary: Officials [say bodies acting across digital, research, data, cybersecurity and regulation have roles not yet articulated in a common steering architecture](2026-07-23-drc-responsible-ai-use-kinshasa-workshop).
developments:
2026-07-23 - the digital economy ministry convened a governance, ethics and regulation panel at which officials [went on the record that bodies already acting across digital, research, data, cybersecurity and regulation have roles not yet sufficiently articulated in a common steering architecture](2026-07-23-drc-responsible-ai-use-kinshasa-workshop).

The base carries no statement of the country's artificial-intelligence governance position before that date, so the direction is withheld and what is stated is where it now stands. No rule, complaint route, audit power or penalty exists for any system operating in the country, including the machine marking of a national examination.

summary: Two regulators [agreed a harmonised reading of the local-content subcontracting texts and joint inspection teams](2026-07-23-cd-arsp-arptc-sous-traitance-telecoms), with scope beyond telecoms.
developments:
2026-07-22 - a first working session at the telecommunications regulator's headquarters [agreed a harmonised reading of the legal texts, joint inspection teams and enforcement of local-content subcontracting rules on large operators, with scope stated beyond telecoms to digital services and electronic commerce](2026-07-23-cd-arsp-arptc-sous-traitance-telecoms).

No written protocol, order or joint communique is held and the account is a news report of the meeting. No inspection has been conducted, no reporting obligation is established, and nothing records an enforcement action since. It is the only instrument on this ledger addressed to what is produced domestically rather than to what is imported or licensed.

The state's own operator is in structural crisis: a directorate-general communique states that [on current finances the company could theoretically pay salaries only every four months, management saying rigour has brought the cycle to every two to two and a half months](2026-06-01-scpt-redressement-communique-rdcmonde), after a [national conference named the sector the state's second-largest revenue source and asset spoliation a problem to fix](2025-10-27-etats-generaux-postes-telecoms-actualite).

summary: A [fourth edition of the Kinshasa digital innovation summit was held on 25 and 26 November 2025](2025-11-27-adis-2025-raissa-malu-education-numerique-actualite), renamed and locally organised.
developments:
Three prior editions ran under a different name in partnership with a Moroccan firm. The fourth was [renamed and localised, organised by a Congolese firm with a fintech-association partnership, an innovation village, free student entry and presidency backing](2025-10-24-lancement-adis-4e-edition-actualite), and [held on 25 and 26 November 2025](2025-11-27-adis-2025-raissa-malu-education-numerique-actualite).

No dates are held for the three earlier editions and no 2026 edition is held. The base carries no incubator, accelerator, fab lab or technology park for this country at all, so an annual conference is the whole of what the indicator can be answered with.

progress: Mixed, start-ups were exempted from the new digital-sector duty schedule while the Startup Act's four implementing decrees stayed in preparation
summary: Start-ups are [fully exempted under Digital Code article 384](2026-08-10-rdc-taxes-numeriques-startups-exonerees-wearetech), while the [Startup Act's implementing texts remain in preparation](2026-08-04-drc-digital-sector-constraints-startup-decree).
developments:
An interministerial order took effect on signature on 20 July 2026 with a [two-tier dollar schedule keyed to whether a provider is judged dominant: cloud services US$5,000 local and US$15,000 foreign in the first tier against US$2,500 and US$10,000 in the second, data-centre declaration from US$25,000 to US$100,000 by tier, and one startup line at US$100](2026-07-20-drc-arrete-interministeriel-015-taux-droits-taxes-redevances-numerique). A [suspension announced on 1 August](2026-08-02-drc-communique-finances-surseance-arrete-015-startups) was [denied on 6 August](2026-08-07-drc-arrete-015-jamais-suspendu-numerico), neither position resting on a published text, and the ministry's 8 August statement [confirmed registered start-ups are fully exempt](2026-08-10-rdc-taxes-numeriques-startups-exonerees-wearetech).

The [four draft decrees adopted in May 2025 to operationalise the 2022 ordinance-law are still in preparation, so no exemption regime for start-ups is in force fifteen months on](2026-08-04-drc-digital-sector-constraints-startup-decree).

summary: A [30-day digital code awareness campaign mobilised 2,000 young volunteers](2026-08-07-drc-digital-code-public-awareness-campaign-launched), and a [cyberviolence ambassadors network launched](2026-08-20-acp-kinshasa-reseau-ambassadeurs-cyberviolences).
developments:
2026-08-06 - a campaign [mobilised 2,000 young volunteers for 30 days at two publications a day on the code's provisions on cybersecurity, data protection and responsible internet use, carried by the digital economy ministry with UN development programme support](2026-08-07-drc-digital-code-public-awareness-campaign-launched). The code was promulgated in March 2023; no budget for the campaign and no measure of its effect is stated.

2026-08-20 - a [national police network of youth ambassadors against digital gender-based violence launched with UN Police and a regional youth leadership chapter, its first session training and certifying 46 people aged 18 to 30 as community prevention relays](2026-08-20-acp-kinshasa-reseau-ambassadeurs-cyberviolences); no budget, coverage target or reporting route is stated.

summary: A [national policy on information technology in education was adopted by the 92nd Council of Ministers](2026-06-15-politique-nationale-ticef-education-actualite), on 19 operational principles.
developments:
2026-06 - the Council of Ministers [adopted a common reference framework for integration, governance, use and regulation of information technology across education, higher education, research, vocational training and literacy, on 19 operational principles in six normative families](2026-06-15-politique-nationale-ticef-education-actualite).

The policy document itself is not held, and no budget, target or implementation step is attached to it in any source held. It is the first education-technology instrument the base records for this country, and nothing since reports a school, a teacher cohort or a device programme delivered under it.

progress: Mixed, an employment and skills platform went live while the digital plan's training targets have no enrolment against them
summary: A [jobseeker and employer platform went live](2026-07-01-onem-mikuba-application-emploi-rdcmonde), while the plan's [250,000-youth training target has no enrolment on record](2026-02-20-drc-500m-digital-transformation-world-bank-afd-techafricanews).
developments:
2026-07 - the employment office [launched a portal and mobile application on which jobseekers register profiles and skills and employers post needs, intended to build a national skills database](2026-07-01-onem-mikuba-application-emploi-rdcmonde); no user, vacancy or placement figure is held.

The plan's human-capital pillar sets [250,000 young people to be trained in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and programming, at least 3,000 in advanced digital skills, about 1,000 teachers in digital literacy and 30,000 cybersecurity jobs, all to 2030](2026-02-20-drc-500m-digital-transformation-world-bank-afd-techafricanews). Six months on, no source establishes a single enrolment against any of them and no budget line funds them.

The measured training on file is [41 certificates awarded at one ceremony, on a programme running since 2017 with about 1,000 girls trained in total](2025-11-05-femintech-41-brevets-ia-informatique-actualite).

summary: The regulator [set a binding complaint escalation path by communique of 22 July 2026](2026-07-24-drc-arptc-telecom-consumer-complaints): 30 working days with the operator, then referral.
developments:
2026-07-22 - a communique signed by the regulator's president [set a binding escalation path: complain to the operator first and allow a maximum of 30 working days, then refer to the regulator by a free line, an online form or physical filing, with a reasoned opinion undertaken within 30 days](2026-07-24-drc-arptc-telecom-consumer-complaints).

The communique itself is not held; the regulator's site is script-rendered and exposes no document path. No complaint volume, opinion or enforcement outcome has been published since, and the tariff changes subscribers report in the east went unannounced without any complaint under the new path reaching the record.

summary: [Fizi Territory has been off calls, SMS and internet since 3 July 2026](2026-08-17-cpj-drc-east-internet-mobile-shutdown-month), and soldiers seized four broadcasters' satellite kits.
developments:
At the window's opening one territory centre was off all networks because [generator fuel could not reach tower sites](2025-03-28-walikale-reseaux-telephonie-coupes-actualite), with [other eastern areas reconnected in February 2026](2026-02-18-rutshuru-masisi-reconnectes-airtel-orange-actualite).

2026-07-03 - [Fizi Territory including Baraka went off calls, SMS and internet and was still cut more than six weeks later amid fighting; soldiers seized the satellite kits of four community broadcasters on 8 July, telling journalists the equipment would be returned only when the war ended, and some outlets have suspended news bulletins](2026-08-17-cpj-drc-east-internet-mobile-shutdown-month), an account [given from Baraka itself](2026-08-03-drc-south-kivu-baraka-fizi-telecoms-blackout-testimony).

No licensing or administrative decision for occupied territory is held, and no restoration date is stated.

progress: Mixed, the universal service fund signed its first subsidy conventions while about 4.3 million people remain uncovered and eastern territories were cut off entirely
summary: The fund [signed subsidy conventions with four operators for 40 localities](2026-08-11-drc-fdsu-mobile-coverage-subsidy-40-localities), against [about 4.3m people with no mobile coverage](2026-08-14-dr-congo-plans-national-strategy-to-expand-mobile-coverage-in-underserved-areas).
developments:
The fund was [created by law in November 2020 and, per a named civil-society officer, still not available](2025-02-19-internet-society-masterclass-fdsu-actualite) at the window's opening. 2026-08-08 - it [signed subsidy conventions with the four operators for a first tranche of 40 localities covering about 258,000 people, with a second phase of 300 sites and a 2030 target of 3,000 localities and 16m people](2026-08-17-portbrief-fdsu-drc-subsidy-agreements); [passive infrastructure stands at fewer than 5,500 towers against an estimated need of at least 30,000](2026-08-19-acp-eaaif-eastcastle-728-pylones-rdc). The phase-0 sites were operator-nominated, ten each, rather than scored on the fund's published index.

A national diagnostic finds [about 4.3 million people in nearly 3,000 localities without mobile coverage, national 2G coverage 77%, 3G 68% and 4G 57%, from about 98% in Kinshasa to 14% in Tshuapa](2026-08-14-dr-congo-plans-national-strategy-to-expand-mobile-coverage-in-underserved-areas).

And a [rural solar base-station commitment of up to 2,000 sites was restated sixteen months on with no sites-built count](2026-05-13-drc-connectivity-improves-usage-power-gaps-connectingafrica).

summary: The second population census reached its cartography phase, run with digital tools and satellite imagery ([broadcast](2026-09-01-cod-cartographie-recensement-numerique-okapi)).
developments:
The census cartography phase is being operationalised with digital tools and satellite imagery, on the central census bureau's technical coordinator's account ([broadcast](2026-09-01-cod-cartographie-recensement-numerique-okapi)).

2026-08-20 - the statistics institute [launched training of trainers in census mapping, with general enumeration scheduled for July 2027](2026-08-20-elitenews-ins-rgph2-cartographie-censitaire). It would be the first census since 1984.

No budget line, financing source, implementing contract or cartography completion figure is held, and the exercise is [framed by the institute as the basis for reliable planning data](2026-07-11-rgph-2-donnees-fiables-planification-actualite). Every population-denominated figure in this report - coverage rates, penetration, inclusion - currently rests on projections from a census forty-two years old.

summary: The statistics institute [launched data.gouv.cd on 23 February 2026](2026-02-23-rhinoceros-data-gouv-cd-lancement).
developments:
[The Institut National de la Statistique launched data.gouv.cd, the national open-data platform, on 23 February 2026, publishing datasets across demography, economy, health, education, public finance, agriculture and infrastructure in CSV, XLSX and JSON](2026-02-23-rhinoceros-data-gouv-cd-lancement).

It is a platform without a governing instrument: no open-data decree, licensing statement, microdata release policy or access-to-information law is held, and no dataset count or usage figure is on the record.

summary: A [contract to supply the RDC-SAT earth-observation satellite was signed in Kinshasa on 16 June 2026](2026-06-17-spacebel-rdc-sat-contract).
developments:
[SPACEBEL signed a contract with the higher education, universities, scientific research and innovation ministry on 16 June 2026 to supply, commission, service and maintain the RDC-SAT earth-observation satellite in support of the National Centre for Remote Sensing, framed as supporting agriculture, mining and forestry monitoring](2026-06-17-spacebel-rdc-sat-contract). [MapBiomas land-cover mapping launched separately in August 2026](2026-08-18-mapbiomas-rdc-lancement).

The satellite is a contracted future capability rather than an operating source: no launch date, cost or data-access arrangement is held.

progress: Mixed, a digital infrastructure and cybersecurity partnership was signed while a US federal claim over a collapsed payments project seeks up to US$400m
summary: A [partnership covering data centres, connectivity, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence was signed in Washington](2026-04-22-cybastion-support-digital-infrastructure-drc-biometricupdate), while a [fintech sued the state](2026-01-19 US fintech sues DR Congo for $400m over failed banking deal).
developments:
2026-04 - a strategic partnership was [signed on the margins of the spring meetings covering data centres, connectivity, cybersecurity, financial technology and artificial intelligence](2026-04-17-cybastion-partners-drc-digital-infrastructure-cybersecurity-techafricanews), with [no value, instrument type, milestones or delivery established](2026-04-22-cybastion-support-digital-infrastructure-drc-biometricupdate) and the exact signing date not stated in either account.

2026-01 - a fintech [filed in a United States federal court against the state and senior officials over the collapsed banking and payments modernisation project, seeking up to US$400m on a stated investment of more than US$72m against an agreed US$20m state contribution never paid, with bribe-demand allegations, the government calling the signed documents a non-binding memorandum and denying the claims](2026-01-19 US fintech sues DR Congo for $400m over failed banking deal). No ruling, docket or government response document is held.

summary: A [US$1.5bn Congo River fibre memorandum was signed](2026-07-03-drc-plans-1-5bn-fibre-congo-river-genew-connectingafrica), and a [police cooperation accord names cybercrime](2026-05-27-accord-cooperation-policiere-chine-cybercriminalite-actualite).
developments:
2026-07 - a memorandum with a Chinese supplier covers [about 2,100 km, 1,700 km along the river plus nearly 400 km terrestrial, at a stated US$1.5bn with more than US$400m required for the first phase, with no financing close, contract or works](2026-07-03-drc-plans-1-5bn-fibre-congo-river-genew-connectingafrica). Both figures are company-reported. It is the country's largest single tracked non-state digital commitment, and it is a memorandum.

2026-05 - an accord signed in Beijing by the interior vice-premier and China's public-security minister [gives Chinese technical assistance to the national police naming cybercrime alongside urban crime and mining fraud, with a standing joint working group](2026-05-27-accord-cooperation-policiere-chine-cybercriminalite-actualite). No text, value, equipment or software list, and no data-handling or oversight arrangement is held.

summary: [Over EUR 180m in new EU and Team Europe investments was announced at the Global Gateway Forum on 9 October 2025](2025-10-09-ec-global-gateway-forum-drc-investments).
developments:
[President von der Leyen met President Tshisekedi at the 2025 Global Gateway Forum on 9 October and announced over EUR 180 million in new EU and Team Europe investments across the Kivu-Kinshasa Green Corridor, Lobito Corridor value chains, Kisangani electrification and critical raw materials cooperation](2025-10-09-ec-global-gateway-forum-drc-investments), building on a [2023 memorandum on critical raw materials](2023-10-26-eu-drc-mou-critical-raw-materials).

None of it names digital regulation, data adequacy or a digital governance instrument, and the base holds no EU financing agreement or delegation statement on any of those.

summary: The digital economy minister [met a Gulf-based delegation on data-centre proposals in February 2026](2026-02-09 DRC steps up talks with foreign firms on data centres and digital infrastructure); talks only.
developments:
2026-02 - the minister [met a Gulf-based delegation on data-centre proposals, with a proposed technical-specification working group and no memorandum, site, capacity or follow-up recorded six months on](2026-02-09 DRC steps up talks with foreign firms on data centres and digital infrastructure).

It is the whole of the relationship as the base holds it. No investment, agreement or presence has followed, and the working group that was proposed has produced nothing on record, so what is stated is an exploratory meeting rather than a commitment.

progress: No change, the relationship is on the record and its digital content is nil
summary: India's [consolidated brief records instruments from 2008 to 2010, none of them digital](2026-02-23-mea-india-drc-bilateral-brief).
developments:
[India's Ministry of External Affairs brief records a 2008 Joint Commission agreement, a 2009 cultural cooperation agreement, a May 2010 memorandum on regular Foreign Office Consultations, decades of ministerial visits, MONUSCO troop contributions and early signature of the International Solar Alliance Agreement](2026-02-23-mea-india-drc-bilateral-brief).

It is India's own authoritative statement of the relationship's standing state, and it names no digital instrument: no line of credit, training placement or supplier contract touching the digital estate is held.
